text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Cyprus will acquire high-technology weapons for effective defence of the island, says President Glafcos Clerides.
- Cancer of the cervix is the most common form of cancer among women in Cyprus.
- Few believe progress on the Cyprus issue can be achieved in the coming months because of the situation in Turkey, reports a Greek newspaper.
- (Leftist) Astra radio station is targetted by arsonists. Communist Akel urges police to speed up inquiries to find the culprits.
- Britain's special envoy on Cyprus Sir David Hannay is working on proposals for Cyprus based on U.N. ideas for the functioning of a future federated state.
- The government will not renew work permits for foreigners in 25 sectors of manufacturing because there are Cypriots unemployed in the same sector.
- Russia is expected to launch an initiative on the Cyprus problem. It proposes the creation of a co-ordination contact commission.
- Chaos in Albania threatens stability in the Balkans.
